newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA'S VODACOM SIGNS HALF MILLION SUBSCRIBERS.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA'S VODACOM SIGNS HALF MILLION SUBSCRIBERS.

text.p: South African mobile telephone company Vodacom announced on Thursday more than 500,000 subscribers were using its network.

Since its establishment in 1994 growth in South Africa's mobile phone industry has exceeded all but the most bullish of forecasts and Vodacom managing director Alan Knott-Craig said the half-a-million milestone had been reached seven years ahead of target.
The firm had experienced a surge in new subscribers in the past two months after the launch of its Vodago product which provides a prepaid billing system.

"To cope with this growth, we are currently still expanding our network at the rate of more than two base stations per day. We are still building coverage in new areas and increasing the capacity of our network," he added.

Vodacom is a joint venture network operator 50 percent owned by South Africa's state telecommunications utility Telkom. Britain's Vodafone Group Plc owns 31.5 percent and Rembrandt Group Ltd holds 18.5 percent.
